title: Jaffe’s critique of Hampton’s supposedly determinate tariff policy
shortTitle: Jaffe’s critique of Hampton’s supposedly determinate tariff policy
summary: Jaffe argues that the cost-equalization formula left substantial administrative choices despite the Court’s presentation of a clear policy.
notes:
Louis Jaffe’s note asks how officials should calculate comparative production costs, including labor, investment, depreciation, and remote foreign production information. Even the goal of equalization might mean preserving existing profit or merely allowing a domestic producer to survive. Presidential initiative and the ability to disregard Commission findings add discretion.

The critique does not change Hampton’s holding. It challenges the descriptive premise that a verbal policy necessarily produces automatic administration, and encourages separating formal statutory guidance from the practical choices required to apply it.
